skill.name: red-team-tools
skill.description: Guides authorized red teams through reconnaissance, web discovery, vulnerability scanning, API enumeration, and reporting workflows using common security tools.
skill.summary: Authorized red-team workflow guide for reconnaissance and bug bounty triage.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static backtick alerts are partly Markdown fence false positives, but several fenced blocks contain real external reconnaissance and scanning commands. The skill is a dual-use red-team guide with active network probing, API fuzzing, Nuclei scanning, and XSS testing guidance, so publication should require strong authorization warnings and safeguards.

remediation.issue: Active scanning and fuzzing workflows can affect third-party systems.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit authorization checkpoint before any active command and require the user to confirm target scope.

remediation.issue: Automated recon examples mix passive and active techniques.
remediation.suggestion: Separate passive OSINT steps from active probing, fuzzing, and vulnerability scanning sections.

remediation.issue: Examples do not consistently show rate limits or concurrency controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add safe defaults for request rates, timeouts, retries, and stop conditions in ffuf, httpx, Dalfox, and Nuclei workflows.

remediation.issue: XSS and API testing examples can be copied to real targets without context.
remediation.suggestion: Label payload and HTTP method examples as authorized testing only and include manual validation steps before reporting.

content.user_title: Run Authorized Red Team Recon Workflows
content.value_statement: Security testers need repeatable recon workflows across many tools. This skill organizes authorized enumeration, vulnerability triage, and reporting steps for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of recon folders, target inputs, and reporting outputs.
Organizes subdomain enumeration with Amass, Subfinder, Assetfinder, and Findomain.
Shows live host discovery and technology fingerprinting with httprobe, httpx, WhatWeb, and Nuclei.
Outlines content and API discovery with ffuf, waybackurls, gau, and wordlists.
Covers XSS hunting and vulnerability scanning workflows with Dalfox and Nuclei.
Provides a sample Bash recon pipeline for authorized domains.
limitations: It does not verify authorization or program scope automatically.
It requires external security tools, a Linux environment, and some API keys.
Scanner output can include false positives and needs manual validation.
Active scans can disrupt services without rate limits and permission.

use_cases.title: Plan Bug Bounty Recon
use_cases.description: Build a scoped recon checklist for approved domains and collect repeatable evidence.

use_cases.title: Map External Attack Surface
use_cases.description: Inventory live hosts, technologies, and exposed paths for owned company assets.

use_cases.title: Triage Web Findings
use_cases.description: Use scanner output and manual checks to prioritize likely vulnerabilities for validation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Passive Recon Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a passive reconnaissance plan for my authorized target. Separate required inputs, tools, outputs, and manual review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Subdomain Enumeration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow design for bug bounty scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a scoped subdomain enumeration workflow for these approved domains. Include deduplication, live host checks, and evidence storage.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Web Testing Areas
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced application review after recon data exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these recon results and prioritize web testing areas. Focus on APIs, uploads, integrations, authentication, and unusual attack surfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Safe Active Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an active scan plan for approved assets. Include rate limits, stop conditions, validation steps, and reporting evidence requirements.

output_examples.input: Plan passive recon for an authorized bug bounty domain.
output: Scope summary with approved domains and exclusions.
Passive data sources to query before active probing.
Output files for subdomains, live hosts, technologies, and notes.
Manual review checklist for high-value assets.

output_examples.input: Prioritize testing after recon finds many live hosts.
output: Group hosts by technology, status code, and exposed application type.
Prioritize login portals, APIs, uploads, admin paths, and integrations.
Flag scanner results that need manual reproduction before reporting.

output_examples.input: Prepare a vulnerability report from validated findings.
output: Finding title, affected asset, impact, reproduction summary, and evidence list.
Severity rationale tied to business impact and exploitability.
Clear remediation steps for engineering teams.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before any active probing or fuzzing.
Start with passive collection, then move to rate-limited active checks.
Manually validate scanner output before reporting a vulnerability.
anti_patterns: Scanning domains, hosts, or endpoints outside the approved scope.
Running brute force or fuzzing workflows on production without permission.
Submitting automated scanner output without reproduction or impact analysis.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only for assets where you have written permission and clear scope.

faq.question: Does the skill install security tools?
faq.answer: No. It describes workflows that require separately installed tools and dependencies.

faq.question: Can it run active scans?
faq.answer: It can guide active scan plans, but execution needs user approval, tools, and authorization.

faq.question: Does it replace manual testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize automation, but findings still need manual validation.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references Amass, Subfinder, httpx, httprobe, ffuf, Nuclei, Dalfox, waybackurls, and related tools.

faq.question: How should results be reported?
faq.answer: Report only validated findings with affected assets, impact, reproduction steps, and remediation guidance.
